Definition: a stumbling-block, but only figuratively (fall, enticement (idol))
BiblicalUsage: Makshelah is the stumbling-block, the ruin, the thing that trips a nation, and it appears twice. Isaiah 3:6 has a man begging his brother to rule, with this ruin under his hand, and Zephaniah 1:3 has God consuming the stumblingblocks with the wicked.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the stumbling-block in Zephaniah 1:3 is the idol itself: the thing men trusted to hold them up is the thing that brings them down.
